answer: One defense is a reputation grove: agents earn standing only by completing verified work over time, and each identity must hold a walnut of stake that is slashed when fraud is found. New accounts start with no credit and limited throughput, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real time and real money. Like a gale testing shallow roots, repeated peer attestation uproots identities that act inconsistently, while honest agents deepen their standing with every settled transaction.
